claims.claim: **Children with EoE tend to eat slowly, gag or choke, regurgitate food, get stuck food or have abdominal pain.** Adolescents and adults report trouble swallowing, food impaction, chest pain on eating, heartburn that does not respond to medicines, and chewing longer or drinking water with solids.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mild reflux with vomiting is usually not EoE.** Most people with EoE have other allergy, such as hay fever or asthma (around 75%).
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Untreated EoE leads to food impaction in around 30-50%,** sometimes needing removal in hospital, and can scar and narrow the oesophagus. Onset in older children and adults usually means lifelong disease.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Confirm the diagnosis by endoscopy with biopsy** (usually by a gastroenterologist). Repeat endoscopy and biopsy are also used to judge treatment response, because symptoms alone may not reflect control.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not do allergy testing for EoE** unless there were rapid allergic symptoms after a food; tests may not predict the effect of diet changes. Pollen immunotherapy is not recommended for EoE.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Care is usually shared between a specialist doctor and a specialist dietitian.** Options: dietary elimination, swallowed corticosteroid (fluticasone puffer, budesonide slurry or dissolving budesonide tablet), a PPI, and dilation for a very narrow oesophagus.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **PPI dose (omeprazole, esomeprazole or lansoprazole, for example):** 10mg twice daily for children of 10-20 kg; 20mg twice daily for children > 20kg; adults 20mg twice daily for the first 2 months, then 20mg once daily.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Swallowed fluticasone starting dose:** 50 ug twice daily at ages one to four; 125 ug twice daily at five to ten; 250 ug twice daily from age ten, including adults. Try halving the dose after the first two to three months.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Swallowed budesonide starting dose:** 0.5 mg twice daily in children and 1mg twice daily in adults; try halving after two to three months, for example by keeping only the night-time dose.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **After swallowed corticosteroid, nothing by mouth for 30 minutes, then rinse** to reduce thrush. Take the evening dose just before bed so the drug stays longer in the oesophagus.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Diet changes are started by a specialist and supervised by a dietitian.** The usual culprits are cow's milk, wheat and egg (soy, seafood and nuts also occur). Approaches: common-allergen elimination (milk, soy, egg, wheat), step-up diets starting with one or two foods, or amino acid formula in babies.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Adrenaline and antihistamines have no role in EoE.** People who also have a food allergy with anaphylaxis risk need a separate anaphylaxis action plan and adrenaline for that allergy.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If symptoms worsen, the specialist is contacted first;** the plan may allow a double dose of swallowed corticosteroid for a set period. Review maintenance therapy after rescue treatment or any food impaction.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **EoE is chronic:** review the plan at every specialist visit.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Signs of food impaction (with vomiting):** food stuck on the way down, chest or oesophageal pain or squeezing, inability to swallow, or needing to spit out saliva or drool.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Call an ambulance (000 in Australia, 111 in New Zealand) or go to an emergency department** when food is still stuck after 1 to 2 hours, or if chest pain is severe with difficulty talking or breathing.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Food impaction options:** nitroglycerin 0.4 mg in 10ml of water by mouth; oral salbutamol 100ug/kg (maximum 5mg); a fizzy drink; or endoscopic removal, ideally with oesophageal biopsies. If it passes on its own, the hospital should still tell the treating doctor.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA eosinophilic oesophagitis resources: EoE Frequently Asked Questions (content updated September 2025), Management Plan for EoE (2025) and Action Plan for EoE (2023)', FAQ and Management Plan 2025; Action Plan 2023, https://www.allergy.org.au/patients/food-other-adverse-reactions/eoe-management-plan, retrieved 2026-09-23
